strings.app.name: SpektraLab
strings.dialog.import.title: Import One or More RAW Photos
strings.dialog.export.title: Export the Displayed Frame · Existing Files Are Not Overwritten
strings.dialog.batch.title: Choose a Folder for Batch Export · Existing Files Are Skipped
strings.navigator.title: Navigator
strings.clipboard.title: Settings Clipboard
strings.clipboard.syncReason: Open a photo and select the photos to sync its settings to in the filmstrip.
strings.film.title: Film
strings.film.reset: Reset the film stock to Portra 400
strings.filmEdge.title: Film Edge
strings.filmEdge.toggleHelp: Print the film around the picture: rebate, holes and edge print
strings.filmEdge.switchOn: Switch Film Edge on in its header.
strings.filmEdge.enterPairLater: Half-frame pairs — two half frames on one piece of film — are coming to Windows.
strings.filmEdge.framing.help: Move the picture under the gate with the crop tool. Return develops; Esc puts it back.
strings.filmEdge.gateUpright: The gate is upright — click for across
strings.filmEdge.gateAcross: The gate is across — click for upright
strings.filmEdge.size:
{0} in a film of about {1}
{2} MP · the border takes no picture pixels
strings.filmEdge.sizeMeasured:
{0} in a film of {1}
{2} MP · the border takes no picture pixels
strings.filmEdge.carrier.help: What a strip scan shows past the film's long edges: nothing, a black carrier or the scan's light
strings.filmEdge.carrier.reason: Only a strip scan reaches past the film's edges.
strings.filmEdge.anotherHelp: Another camera body: a new gate, new margins and new holes
strings.filmEdge.anotherFrameHelp: Another frame of the same roll: a new advance and a new scan
strings.filmEdge.lensExif: Lens f/{0}, from EXIF: the gate's softness.
strings.filmEdge.lensAssumed: Lens f/5.6, assumed: EXIF has no aperture. It sets the gate's softness.
strings.dateBack.title: Date Back
strings.dateBack.toggleHelp: Expose the date onto the negative, as a camera's date back did
strings.dateBack.switchOn: Switch Date Back on in its header.
strings.dateBack.orderHelp: The order the date is written in
strings.dateBack.source.help: Print the shooting date from the RAW, or a date you type
strings.dateBack.typedHelp: The line to print, as you type it: up to 32 characters. Return applies it.
strings.dateBack.withDataWhere: beside the frame, with the date
strings.dateBack.withDataHelp: Print the shooting data beside the frame as well as the date
strings.dateBack.marginNote: On 120 the date prints in the film margin beside the frame.
strings.dateBack.turned: It turned for this frame, so the date runs down the picture.
strings.dateBack.level: It was held level, so the date runs along the picture.
strings.dateBack.noCamera: Film Format is no camera with a date back: 135, half frame or 645 has one; other 120 formats need Film Edge.
strings.dateBack.panoramic: No date back on the panoramic formats.
strings.dateBack.dataNeedsEdge120: A 120 back prints beside the frame, on the film edge: it needs Film Edge.
strings.dateBack.dataNeedsEdge: Data prints beside the frame, on the film edge: it needs Film Edge.
strings.print.title: Print
strings.print.slideScannedDirectly: A slide film is scanned directly, without a paper.
strings.print.reason.slideFilm: A slide film is already a positive — there is nothing for a paper to interpret. It is scanned directly.
strings.print.reason.noScanNegative: Scanning a negative without a print is not available on Windows yet.
strings.print.edrScope: Changes the render — canvas, proof and file alike
strings.print.fastFlip: Fast flip (baked LUT, no glare, ignores your print grade)
strings.crop.title: Crop
strings.crop.dragToCrop: Drag on the Picture to Crop
strings.crop.editingNote: Drag a rectangle on the unrotated original; orientation and straightening return when you finish. Enter confirms, Esc cancels.
strings.crop.sharedNote: Preview and export use the same crop and orientation; the original RAW is never changed.
strings.crop.waitForEditor: Finish or cancel the crop on the canvas first (Enter / Esc).
strings.crop.heldReason: Film Edge frames the picture in its gate. Switch it off to crop.
strings.crop.straightenNote: Straightening applies when you release the slider. The edges tighten automatically so no blank corners show.
strings.enlarger.title: Enlarger
strings.enlarger.reset: Reset the enlarger to the solved pack
strings.enlarger.reason.slide: A slide film is scanned directly; there is no print to expose or filter.
strings.toolbar.undoHelp: Undo the last adjustment to this photo · Ctrl+Z
strings.toolbar.redoHelp: Redo the adjustment to this photo · Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y
strings.toolbar.cropHelp: Crop — drag a rectangle on the picture
strings.toolbar.zoomFitted: Fitted to the window — {0} % (Ctrl+0). Click for 100 %; right-click for the zoom menu.
strings.toolbar.zoomActual: 100 % — one screen pixel per photo pixel (Ctrl+1). Click to fit; right-click for the zoom menu.
strings.canvas.emptyHint: Import RAW photos and choose a film and paper for each
strings.strip.syncHelp: Apply this photo's film, paper, decode and effects to the selected photos. The crop is not synced.
strings.strip.selectHelp: Include in the selection that Sync and batch export use (Ctrl+click)
strings.strip.empty: Drop RAW photos here, or press Ctrl+O.
strings.latitude.title: Latitude
strings.camera.title: Input / Camera
strings.camera.filmExposureNote: Where the scene sits on the film's curve, in stops: grain, latitude and saturation move; the print is re-timed to it. Each photo's settings save automatically.
strings.camera.pickNeutral: Pick a neutral point on the image
strings.format.title: Film Format
strings.format.note: The physical format's long edge sets the scale of grain and halation; cropping does not change the format.
strings.format.reset: Reset the film format and its effects
strings.format.resetStrengths: Reset effect strengths to the film's own
strings.effect.reasonOff: The effect is off; its strength is kept for when it comes back on.
strings.placement.title: Scene Placement
strings.mask.title: Tone Mask
strings.mask.caption: Change in paper exposure against the blurred negative, stops
strings.decode.title: RAW Decode
strings.decode.compatibleNote: Matches the validated native RAW pipeline.
strings.decode.headroomNote: Keeps some highlights and negative values after demosaicing; demosaicing is still integer.
strings.info.title: Photo Info
strings.status.title: Status
strings.status.closing: Closing once the current operation finishes…
strings.placeholder.process: Process — auto-exposure and the enlarger filter pack for this paper — is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.original: Showing the original RAW before the film simulation is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.compare: The before / after split is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.latitude: The latitude graph — the scene in stops against this film and paper — is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.asShot: Film exposure as shot is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.whiteBalance: Decode white balance is coming to the Windows RAW decode.
strings.placeholder.lensCorrection: Lens correction is coming to the Windows RAW decode.
strings.placeholder.antihalation: Removing the film's anti-halation layer is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.scenePlacement: Scene Placement is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.toneMask: The Tone Mask is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.printEffects: Switching the print effects (glare, pre-flash) off in one place is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.edr: Extended Dynamic Range print profiles are coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.digitalIntermediate: The Digital Intermediate — the negative with its orange mask removed and reversed on the film's own neutral curve — is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.clipboard: Copying and pasting chosen groups of settings is coming to Windows; Sync copies this photo's settings now.
strings.export.title: Export Photos
strings.export.intro:
The displayed frame or the selected photos · sRGB
The crop and effects are written into the file.
strings.export.sizeNote: Keeps the aspect ratio and never enlarges. PNG is lossless; JPEG is lossy.
strings.export.note: Exporting the displayed frame never overwrites a file. A batch export works one photo at a time and skips names that already exist; photos you have not opened render with their own settings.
strings.status.ready: Ready · open a RAW file to begin
strings.status.opening: Decoding and rendering the RAW file…
strings.status.previewCurrent: Preview already shows the current settings
strings.status.batchFinished: Batch export finished: {0} exported, {1} skipped (file exists), {2} failed
strings.status.batchCancelled: Batch export cancelled: {0} exported, {1} skipped (file exists), {2} failed
strings.status.syncedKeepingCrops: Photos synced: {0} (each keeps its own crop).
strings.status.undone: Undid the last adjustment to this photo
strings.status.redone: Redid the adjustment to this photo
strings.saved.unsaved: Some settings are not saved; see the warning below
strings.saved.automatic: Adjustments save automatically and return when the photo is reopened
strings.saved.newerFields: · {0} settings from a newer version are not used here and are kept as they are
